partners.mechanism_chain: HNF1B (HGNC:4892) —LEADS_TO→ Pancreatic agenesis (HP:0002055); HNF1B (HGNC:4892) —LEADS_TO→ Neonatal diabetes mellitus (HP:0011102); HNF1B (HGNC:4892) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebellar agenesis (HP:0001317); HNF1B (HGNC:4892) —LEADS_TO→ Renal cysts (HP:0000100); HNF1B (HGNC:4892) —LEADS_TO→ Diabetes mellitus (HP:0000822). Haploinsufficiency of the HNF1B gene leads to developmental defects impacting multiple organs. In the context of permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus-pancreatic and cerebellar agenesis syndrome, HNF1B dysfunction results in pancreatic agenesis, neonatal diabetes mellitus, and cerebellar agenesis. In renal cysts and diabetes syndrome, HNF1B haploinsufficiency causes renal cysts and diabetes mellitus. The shared gene and overlapping phenotypes point to a common developmental pathway disrupted by HNF1B deficiency.

#### 1. pancreatic agenesis 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.731)

Loss-of-function mutations in PTF1A disrupt the critical pathway of pancreas development, leading to pancreatic agenesis. In the case of permanent neonatal diabetes mellitus-pancreatic and cerebellar agenesis syndrome, this disruption also extends to cerebellar development, resulting in cerebellar agenesis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in PTF1A with a demonstrably gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, or the absence of any PTF1A variants in individuals with these phenotypes, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome Variant Server (EVS) or gnomAD data showing a high frequency (>1%) of loss-of-function variants in PTF1A in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PTF1A in these distinct but overlapping conditions can inform therapeutic strategies aimed at promoting pancreatic and cerebellar development or mitigating the consequences of agenesis, potentially through gene therapy or regenerative medicine approaches targeting the PTF1A pathway.
